author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey proposed new spending and regulatory changes Tuesday aimed at identifying postpartum mental-health concerns earlier and connecting more families with care.

Healey plans to seek $2 million in a supplemental budget to expand the Department of Public Health’s Welcome Family program statewide. The program offers parents and caregivers a free, one-time home visit from a maternal and child health nurse during the first weeks after a birth.

The governor’s office says Welcome Family currently serves about 3,000 births a year, compared with roughly 68,000 births statewide. The proposed appropriation would make a visit available to every parent or caregiver, though lawmakers must approve the funding.

A separate $250,000 proposal would strengthen the Massachusetts Child Psychiatry Access Program for Moms, which helps clinicians address perinatal mental-health needs. The Department of Public Health also plans to revise regulations governing screening for mood and anxiety disorders during and after pregnancy.
dek: Gov. Maura Healey is seeking $2.25 million to broaden newborn home visits and strengthen a clinician-consultation program, alongside planned screening-rule changes.
headline: Massachusetts proposes expanded postpartum mental-health support
